payload.headline: AMD bounces 5.31% to 530.14; strong growth, but price stays far above value

summary.thesis: AMD's business is growing fast with rising margins, but at 530.14 the stock trades well above every fair-value estimate in our data, which tops out at 333.38.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, because the price is above the whole valuation range. Swing: wait, because resistance is less than one average daily move above the close.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38; swing setup needs a close above 562.99

payload.happening: AMD rose 5.31% to close at 530.14, just above the top of its 517.35–530.13 support zone. There is no news since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
payload.business: Three things change the business, and all of them are improving. Demand: trailing 12-month revenue is 45.4B, up from 32.0B, and quarterly growth sped up to 44.68% year on year from 37.85% two quarters ago. Margins: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Cash: free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 7.1B from 5.4B, and net cash is 8.7B, so the balance sheet is not at risk. Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates 11.3% in the last 30 days. The filings flag two business risks. Inventory is up 57% while latest-quarter sales are up 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. The 18% operating margin also sits near the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%, and peaks like that usually fade. Other signals affect only mood: the macro agent reports a tech market in a downtrend with elevated fear, and options imply volatility of 107.6. Segment data is not available, so we can't tell which product lines drive the growth. Competition from peers such as NVDA and AVGO is a factor (general knowledge), but our data has no market-share figures.

worth.text: AMD trades at 115.6 times trailing earnings, 65.6 times this year's estimate and 30.1 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio (market value divided by yearly revenue) is 19.1, against a peer median of 13.1, and that sits at the 90th percentile of AMD's own 5-year history. A discounted cash-flow model values the future cash the business is expected to produce in today's money, using a discount rate of 10.1%. It gives 143.15 in the bear case, 183.08 in the base case and 215.93 in the bull case. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. The two methods differ most because of how fast cash flow is assumed to grow at the start. The model caps starting growth at 30%, which gives 183.92, while analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 118%. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 13%, the value drops to 97.11. Even the most generous number in our data, 333.38, is well below 530.14. The price assumes growth stays far above anything the model allows for years.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the model caps it at 30% (value 183.92), while analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 118%, and only growth well beyond the cap could justify 530.14.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly revenue grew 44.68% year on year, up from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability is rising: operating margin is 17.72%, up from 8.78%, and free cash flow grew to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Analysts are raising forecasts: the next-year EPS estimate is 17.64, up 11.3% in 30 days, which brings the next-year P/E down to 30.1.
bear: The price is above every valuation: 530.14 compares with a top fair value of 333.38 and a DCF base of 183.08.
The stock is expensive relative to peers and its own history: price-to-sales is 19.1, against a peer median of 13.1, and sits at the 90th percentile of its own 5-year range.
Margins may already be at a peak: inventory is up 57% while sales are up 45%, and if operating margin fell to 13% the model value would drop to 97.11.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 480.33–502.6 support zone. A close below it would break the trading range, but the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, at the high end of AMD's own price-to-sales history. The valuation case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is getting stronger, but the price needs growth well beyond the model's 30% cap. The highest fair value in our data is 333.38.

swing.why: The close of 530.14 cleared the top of the support zone (530.13) by a hair. Resistance starts at 546.44, less than one ATR (average daily range) of 40.33 away, and the 50-day average of 555.22 sits inside that resistance zone, so the upside is small next to normal daily swings. A cleaner setup needs a close above 562.99.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are still far off, but options imply moves of 9.0% by 2026-11-20 and 18.1% by 2026-12-18, and actual volatility (125.3) is running above implied volatility (107.6), so large swings can come before the report.

change_mind: A drop to 333.38, the top of the fair-value range, would turn the long-term call from wait to buy, provided operating margin holds near 17.72%.
A close above 562.99 would clear resistance and the 50-day average of 555.22, which would create a swing entry. A close below 480.33 would break the range and rule out a long swing.
If the next report on 2027-02-02 shows operating margin falling toward 13% (model value 97.11), or the next-year EPS estimate of 17.64 drops back toward 15.85, the bull case weakens.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; the 5.31% bounce to 530.14 left the price above every valuation value, the highest being 333.38.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
